findings.title: Callable aliases and dynamic builtin indirection bypass the lineage scanner
assumptions: The spec's fail_closed_on production_import_or_resolvable_call requirement covers semantically resolvable aliases and dynamic builtin access, not only direct ast.Call names.
A negative scanner probe may use a temporary file outside the worktree without changing repository state.

reproduction.environment: Python 3.12.3, repository venv, git HEAD e77510170424eecd49112ed6c33424ce455b154c
reproduction.command_summary: Import the PR-123 builder and call _automated_scan_checks(path, {'mv_weights'}) on three temporary snippets: g=getattr followed by g(obj,'mv_weights')(x); alias=mv_weights followed by alias(x); and __builtins__['getattr'](obj,'mv_weights')(x).
reproduction.expected: At least one scanner check must be false for every snippet.

findings.source: _automated_scan_checks records only direct ast.Name/ast.Attribute callees. It does not propagate assignments that alias forbidden symbols or dynamic builtins, and it does not recognize subscripted builtins access.
findings.consequence: A reference can call a mapped production implementation while receiving an all-green automated_scan_checks record. The generated all_rows_valid=true and PASS_MECHANICS_C2 lineage status therefore overstate the enforced independence guarantee.
findings.required_fix: Add fail-closed alias/dataflow handling or conservatively reject callable aliasing and dynamic builtin access in reference closures. Add negative tests for direct aliases, getattr aliases, imported dynamic-call aliases, and __builtins__ subscript access; then regenerate and replay all PR-123 artifacts.
